question:
A 48-year-old woman presents with left leg swelling that began following a transcontinental flight.
Duplex ultrasound of the left leg reveals a noncompressible popliteal vein. She is prescribed a
medication that inhibits the coagulation cascade. Two weeks later, her laboratory results are as follows:
| Laboratory Parameter | Result | |------------------------------|-------------------| | Platelet count | 210,000/mm3
| | Partial thromboplastin time | 53 seconds | | Prothrombin time | 20 seconds | | Thrombin time | 15
seconds (control: 15 seconds) | Which of the following medications was most likely prescribed? Answer
Choices: (A) Dabigatran (B) Edoxaban (C) Low molecular weight heparin (D) Bivalirudin (E) Apixaban
(F) Unfractionated heparin (G) Rivaroxaban (H) Fondaparinux (I) Warfarin (J) Argatroban
 A. Fondaparinux
B. Rivaroxaban
C. Bivalirudin
D. Apixaban
E. Low molecular weight heparin
F. Argatroban
G. Unfractionated heparin
H. Warfarin
I. Edoxaban
J. Dabigatran
